claims.statement: Every service exposes one health dialect: GET /health/live (process liveness), GET /health/ready (DB reachable + master key loads, 200 {"status":"ok"} or 503 {"status":"degraded"}), and a deprecated /health alias of readiness; all three are @Public and return only the status JSON.
Readiness deliberately does not check Redis or RabbitMQ: both are fail-open on the HTTP path, so their outage must never take a service out of rotation.
AuthGuard verifies bearer tokens and installs the principal; @Public routes skip it, and the NODE_ENV=development bypass covers only credential-less requests — a presented token is always verified.

Cursor paging lives in one seam (opaque cursor codec, default limit 50, max 200); each caller supplies its own stable sort key and strictly-after test, and the module decrypts nothing and sorts nothing.

An Outbox row is one 'tell another service' intent inserted in the same transaction as its business row, so a committed write can never lose its notification and a rolled-back one can never send it; delivery is at-least-once because publishedAt is written only by the poller.
The outbox poller delivers rows sequentially (one failing row cannot abort or reorder the batch) and advances its cursor only after the broker confirms; each sweep is bounded.
Origin grants are the enforcement point for outside surfaces creating/ticking todos: the grant is written before an intent is enqueued, and a toggle flag is convenience only.
